mainTopic: Washing hands before תפילה, and whether one must hear his own קריאת שמע (רבי יוסי vs. רבי יהודה), applied to a חרש's תרומה, ברכת המזון, and מגילה
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יוחנן's teaching on accepting a complete מלכות שמים: relieve oneself, wash hands, put on תפילין, say קריאת שמע, and daven. Doing this is compared to building a מזבח and bringing a קרבן, and רבא adds that it is even like טבילה. A scholar from ארץ ישראל rules that without water one may wipe his hands with anything that cleans, and רבא agrees, since the פסוק says בנקיון, not 'water'. The גמרא then limits this: for קריאת שמע one need not search for water, but for תפילה one must go up to a פרסה ahead, or back less than a מיל. A new משנה follows about saying שמע without hearing oneself, without precise letters, out of order, or with a mistake. The גמרא explains how רבי יוסי and the תנא קמא each read the word ״שמע״. Next it tries to match the rule about a חרש separating תרומה to רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה, working through ברייתות about ברכת המזון and about a חרש separating תרומה, and it settles them by splitting views between רבי יהודה, his teacher, and רבי מאיר. Finally, a משנה in מגילה disqualifying a חרש is attributed by רב מתנה to רבי יוסי, and the גמרא begins to question this. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The order of a complete acceptance of Heaven's kingship
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יוחנן's teaching: relieve oneself, wash hands, put on תפילין, say קריאת שמע, daven. This is complete מלכות שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should relieve himself, wash his hands, put on תפילין, read קריאת שמע, and daven. That is the complete acceptance of the Kingdom of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement of רבי יוחנן that began on the previous daf. It lists the steps for someone who wants to accept עול מלכות שמים in the fullest way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the order. First he makes his body clean (relieving himself, washing hands), then he puts on תפילין, then he says קריאת שמע, and finally he davens. Doing all of these together is what makes the acceptance 'complete' (שלמה).

keyTerms.meaning: He should relieve himself (go to the bathroom)
תפילין, worn on the arm and head
Complete acceptance of the Kingdom of Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new teaching. It is the second half of a sentence from the previous daf ('one who wants to accept upon himself עול מלכות שמים in full...').

phrases.english: He should relieve himself, and wash his hands,
phrases.notes: Continuation of רבי יוחנן's statement from 14b

phrases.english: and put on tefillin,
and read Shema, and pray,
and this is the complete Kingdom of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The full sequence of relieving oneself, washing, תפילין, קריאת שמע and תפילה constitutes complete acceptance of מלכות שמים.

steps.title: Doing these steps is like building an altar and bringing an offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: whoever follows this order is credited as if he built a מזבח and offered a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who relieves himself, washes his hands, puts on תפילין, reads קריאת שמע, and davens, the פסוק considers him as if he built a מזבח and brought a קרבן on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from רבי יוחנן, about the same set of actions, now describes the reward. The person is treated as if he built a מזבח and brought a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first statement told us what these actions accomplish: complete מלכות שמים. This one adds how much they are worth. Preparing properly and then davening is compared to the קרבנות in the בית המקדש. The source פסוק comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse credits him / considers him

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who relieves himself, and washes his hands,
and puts on tefillin, and reads Shema,
and prays —
the verse credits him
as if he built an altar
and offered a sacrifice upon it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching of רבי יוחנן about the same sequence, describing its spiritual worth
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preparing properly and then davening is considered like building a מזבח and offering a קרבן.

steps.title: The verse: I will wash my hands and circle Your altar
steps.stepSummary: The source is תהלים: 'I will wash my hands in cleanliness, and I will circle Your מזבח, ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'I will wash my hands in cleanliness, and I will go around Your מזבח, ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that supports רבי יוחנן's comparison to a מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts washing hands right next to going around the מזבח. That pairing shows that washing before serving ה׳ through תפילה is linked to the service of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will go around / encircle

phrases.english: as it is written:
"I will wash in purity my hands,
and I will encircle Your altar, O Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: אֶרְחַץ בְּנִקָּיוֹן כַּפָּי וַאֲסוֹבְבָה אֶת מִזְבַּחֲךָ ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for step 2
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that washing and davening is like building a מזבח and bringing a קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים כו:ו, which places hand-washing next to circling the מזבח

steps.title: רבא adds: it is even as if he immersed
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is also as if he did טבילה (immersed his whole body), because the פסוק says ארחץ ('I will wash myself') and not ארחיץ כפי ('I will wash my hands').
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Don't you hold, Master, that it is as if he immersed? For it is written 'ארחץ' (I will wash myself), and it is not written 'ארחיץ' (I will wash my hands).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds to the praise. Washing hands before davening counts as if the person immersed his whole body in a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is grammatical. ארחץ means 'I will wash myself', which sounds like the whole body. ארחיץ would mean 'I will cause my hands to be washed', meaning just the hands. Since the פסוק chose the 'whole self' form, it treats the hand-washing as a full טבילה. This is an expansion of רבי יוחנן's teaching, not an attack on it.

keyTerms.meaning: I will cause to be washed (used for washing a body part, like hands)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though it is phrased as a question ('don't you hold?'), רבא is not disagreeing. He is adding a further level of praise: not only like a קרבן, but also like טבילה.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Does the Master not hold
that it is as if he immersed,
as it is written: "I will wash [in purity]" —
phrases.notes: ארחץ = I will wash myself (whole body)

phrases.english: and it does not write "I will wash [my hands]".

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר כְּאִילּוּ טָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further derivation from the same פסוק, expanding the reward
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing hands before davening is considered as if one immersed his entire body.

steps.title: A surprising ruling: wiping hands without water
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רבא about a young scholar from ארץ ישראל who ruled that someone without water may wipe his hands with earth, a pebble, or a wood chip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: Look, Master, at this young scholar who came from the West (ארץ ישראל) and said: Someone who has no water to wash his hands may wipe his hands with earth, a pebble, or a wood chip.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא reports a ruling he finds surprising and asks רבא, in effect, whether it is correct. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that washing hands before davening matters a great deal. So it seems strange that someone could get by with no water at all. רבינא wants to know whether wiping with dry materials is really good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Look, Master (see what this one says)
A splinter or chip of wood

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Let the Master see
this young Torah scholar
who came from the West (Eretz Yisrael) and said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַיִם לִרְחוֹץ יָדָיו —
phrases.english: one who has no water to wash his hands —
wipes his hands with earth,
or with a pebble, or with a wood chip.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא: חֲזִי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a practical question about hand-washing, related to the פסוק just discussed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the scholar's ruling right, that dry wiping can replace washing with water before תפילה?

steps.title: רבא approves: the verse says 'cleanliness', not 'water'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the scholar is right. The פסוק says בנקיון ('in cleanliness'), not 'with water', so anything that cleans is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: He spoke well. Does it say 'I will wash with water'? It says 'in cleanliness', meaning anything that cleans.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבינא's question. The ruling is correct, and he proves it from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the word בנקיון closely. The פסוק does not require water specifically. It requires that the hands become clean. So earth, a pebble, or a wood chip work when water is not available.

keyTerms.meaning: He spoke well / he is correct
Is it written…? (rhetorical: it is not)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: when no water is available, one may clean his hands with something else before davening.

phrases.english: He said to him: He spoke well,
is it written "I will wash with water"?
"In purity" is written —
anything that cleans,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבינא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The פסוק requires cleanliness (בנקיון), not water, so anything that cleans the hands is valid.

steps.title: Support from רב חסדא: don't chase water at prayer time
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his answer with רב חסדא, who cursed anyone who goes out searching for water at the time of תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב חסדא would curse anyone who goes looking for water at the time of davening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his answer with the practice of רב חסדא. Searching for water when it is time to daven was strongly opposed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If water were absolutely required, it would make sense to go look for it. רב חסדא cursed anyone who did that at the time of תפילה. This shows that another cleaning method is acceptable, and that davening on time comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: Washing hands before davening is so valuable that it counts like a קרבן and like טבילה. Still, the requirement is cleanliness (בנקיון), not water. If no water is available, anything that cleans is enough. רב חסדא's curse on searching for water is limited in the next step: it applies to קריאת שמע, but for תפילה one must search.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not against washing with water. He objects to going out searching for water when it means pushing off davening at its time.

phrases.english: for indeed Rav Chisda
would curse one
who goes around searching for water
at the time of prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא רַב חִסְדָּא לָיֵיט אַמַּאן דִּמְהַדַּר אַמַּיָּא בְּעִידָּן צְלוֹתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings supporting evidence for רבא's answer
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that anything that cleans is enough, and water is not required
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's curse on someone who searches for water at the time of תפילה

steps.title: The curse applies only to קריאת שמע, not to תפילה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's curse on searching for water applies only to קריאת שמע. For תפילה, one must search for water.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only applies to קריאת שמע. But for תפילה, he must go looking for water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on רב חסדא's curse from the last step. Searching for water is wrong only when it comes to קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע has a fixed time limit, so if you go looking for water you might miss it. תפילה can be said over a longer stretch of time, so there is time to search for water. This is why searching is required for תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply (only to…): a formula that limits an earlier rule
He goes searching / goes out of his way

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה: the rule that you do not need water applies only to שמע. Before תפילה, you must make an effort to wash with water.

phrases.english: And this applies only to the recitation of Shema,
phrases.notes: קריאת שמע has a deadline; searching could make him miss it.

phrases.english: but for prayer, he must search (for water).
phrases.notes: תפילה has a longer time window.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, אֲבָל לִתְפִלָּה מְהַדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רב חסדא's curse quoted in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no need to search for water for קריאת שמע, but one must search for water for תפילה.

steps.title: How far must one go to find water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far a person must go to look for water for תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how far must he go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the rule it just gave. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know a person must search for water for תפילה, we need a limit. Otherwise he could be expected to walk forever.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much? (asking for a measurement)

phrases.english: And how far (must he go)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measurement of the obligation stated in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum distance a person must travel to find water for תפילה.

steps.title: Up to a פרסה
steps.stepSummary: A person must go up to a פרסה to find water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to a פרסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the limit is one פרסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרסה is a fixed distance, equal to four מיל. This gives a clear limit to how much effort is required.

keyTerms.meaning: A פרסה (parasang), a distance equal to four מיל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up פרסה and מיל. A פרסה is four times longer than a מיל, and both measurements come up in the next steps.

phrases.english: Up to a parasang (parsa).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One must go up to a פרסה to find water.

steps.title: A פרסה ahead, but not even a מיל backward
steps.stepSummary: The פרסה rule applies only to water ahead of him. He does not have to go back even one מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only ahead of him. But behind him, he does not go back even a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit. The direction he is traveling matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking ahead is on his way, so it is less of a burden. Going backward means undoing his trip, so the required distance is much shorter: less than one מיל.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of him (on his way)
A מיל, about 2,000 אמות; a quarter of a פרסה

phrases.english: And this applies only in front of him,
but behind him —
he does not go back even a mil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the פרסה rule from step 10 to forward travel only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He must go a פרסה forward, but need not go back even one מיל.

steps.title: Less than a מיל backward, he must go back
steps.stepSummary: From the wording, we learn that he must go back for water that is less than a מיל behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this we learn: it is a full מיל that he does not go back. But less than a מיל, he does go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the exact words of the last step. This closes the section about searching for water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'he does not go back a מיל' implies that a shorter distance is different. So if water is less than a מיל behind him, he must go back for it.
steps.whatToRemember: For תפילה: search for water up to a פרסה ahead, and go back for it if it is less than a מיל behind. For קריאת שמע, do not search at all; cleaning hands with anything is enough.

phrases.english: From this: it is a mil that he does not go back,
but less than a mil — he does go back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Water that is less than a מיל behind him: he must go back for it.

steps.title: משנה: שמע not audible to one's own ear
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if someone said שמע without hearing it himself, he fulfilled his obligation. רבי יוסי disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says שמע but not loud enough for his own ear to hear, he has fulfilled his obligation. רבי יוסי says: he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about how שמע must be said. The first case is saying it too quietly to hear yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first, unnamed opinion (the תנא קמא) holds that saying the words is enough, even without hearing them. רבי יוסי holds that you must say it loud enough for your own ear to hear.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
Made it heard to his own ear
He did not fulfill his obligation

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאׇזְנוֹ — יָצָא.
phrases.english: One who recites Shema and did not make it audible to his own ear — fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: This is the anonymous first opinion (תנא קמא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאׇזְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה; it is not connected to the water discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, שמע said too quietly for him to hear is still valid. According to רבי יוסי, it is invalid.

steps.title: משנה: not saying the letters precisely
steps.stepSummary: If someone did not say the letters of שמע precisely, רבי יוסי says he fulfilled his obligation. רבי יהודה says he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone read שמע but was not careful with its letters, רבי יוסי says: he has fulfilled his obligation. רבי יהודה says: he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: saying שמע without pronouncing the letters carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about clear pronunciation, for example not blurring the end of one word into the start of the next. רבי יוסי is lenient here, while רבי יהודה requires precise letters.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is strict in the first case (he must hear himself) but lenient in this one (precise letters are not required). These are two separate questions, so his opinions are not contradicting each other.

phrases.english: One who recited and was not precise in its letters,
Rabbi Yosei says: he fulfilled his obligation.
Rabbi Yehuda says: he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, imprecise letters are still valid. According to רבי יהודה, they are invalid.

steps.title: משנה: reading out of order, and fixing a mistake
steps.stepSummary: Reading שמע out of order does not count. If someone made a mistake, he goes back to the place of the mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone reads שמע out of order, he has not fulfilled his obligation. If he read and made a mistake, he goes back to the place where he made the mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with two more rules: the order of שמע must be kept, and a mistake is fixed by going back to where it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying שמע out of order (למפרע) makes it invalid. However, one mistake does not ruin the whole reading. He only needs to go back to the point of the error, not to the very beginning.
steps.whatToRemember: The order of שמע is essential. If he makes a mistake, he goes back only to the place of the mistake, not to the start.

phrases.english: One who recites out of order — did not fulfill his obligation.
One who recited and erred —
should return to the place where he erred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final cases in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading out of order is invalid. After a mistake, he returns to the place of the mistake.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source behind רבי יוסי's view that one must hear his own שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking why רבי יוסי says you must hear your own קריאת שמע. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי said that if someone did not hear himself, he did not fulfill his obligation. The גמרא now wants the source in the פסוק for that requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The תנא who requires hearing one's own שמע

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the מחלוקת in the משנה (step 13) and asks for רבי יוסי's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק-based reason that one must hear his own recitation of שמע.

steps.title: The word ״שמע״ means: make your ear hear
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reads ״שמע״ literally: your ear must hear what your mouth says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written ״שמע״ ('hear'): make your ear hear what you bring out of your mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי learns from the word ״שמע״ itself. 'Hear' means you must actually hear the words you are saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי takes the word ״שמע״ at face value, as an instruction to hear. So saying the words without hearing them is not enough, even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: For it is written (in the פסוק)
What you bring out of your mouth (what you say)

phrases.english: Because it is written: 'Hear' —
make your ear hear
what you bring out of your mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״שמע״ teaches that one must hear with his ears what he says with his mouth.

steps.title: The תנא קמא reads ״שמע״ as 'any language you understand'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses the word ״שמע״ for a different lesson: שמע may be said in any language one understands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא holds: ״שמע״ means in any language that you understand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא קמא does not require hearing. He uses the word ״שמע״ for a different lesson: you may say קריאת שמע in any language you understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here ״שמע״ means 'understand', not 'hear with your ears'. Since the word is already used for the language rule, the תנא קמא has no source that requires hearing, so one who did not hear himself still fulfilled his obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: In this step ״שמע״ means 'understand', not 'hear with your ears'. The same word is being read two different ways.

phrases.english: And the first tanna holds: 'Hear' —
in any language that you understand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reading of the same word explained in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, ״שמע״ teaches that קריאת שמע may be said in any language one understands, not that one must hear himself.

steps.title: רבי יוסי learns both lessons from ״שמע״
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי agrees about language, and also learns the hearing rule from the same word.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי: learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: what does רבי יוסי do with the language rule? He learns both lessons from the one word ״שמע״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think רבי יוסי rejects the language rule, since he used ״שמע״ for hearing. The גמרא says no: he accepts that שמע may be said in any language, and also requires hearing. The real disagreement is only whether the word can carry two lessons.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree שמע may be said in any language. They disagree only about hearing: רבי יוסי learns both rules from ״שמע״, and the תנא קמא learns only the language rule.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei —
learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles how רבי יוסי deals with the תנא קמא's reading from step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי might reject the 'any language' rule, since he used ״שמע״ for hearing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי derives both rules, any language and hearing oneself, from ״שמע״.

steps.title: A deaf person who speaks should not separate תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in תרומות: a deaf person who speaks but cannot hear should not separate תרומה at the start, but if he did, it counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: a deaf person who speaks but does not hear should not separate תרומה. But if he did separate, his תרומה is valid תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכתא about a deaf person who can speak. This sets up the next question, which links it to our מחלוקת about hearing one's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומה needs a ברכה, and this person cannot hear his own ברכה. So at the start he should not separate, but after the fact his תרומה is still valid. This is the same hearing question as in קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
A deaf person who speaks but cannot hear
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: We learned there:
A deaf person who speaks but does not hear —
should not separate teruma.
And if he did separate —
his teruma is teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה that touches the same hearing issue as the מחלוקת in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש who speaks should not separate תרומה at the start, but if he did, it is valid תרומה.

steps.title: Which תנא holds 'valid after the fact, not at the start'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the תרומה משנה follows: after the fact it is valid, but at the start it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that for a deaf person who speaks but does not hear, after the fact, yes, it counts, but at the start, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the תרומה משנה follows. This sets up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that neither side in our משנה fits neatly. The תנא קמא seems to allow not hearing even at the start, and רבי יוסי seems to say it does not count even after the fact. The גמרא is looking for a view that matches the middle position of 'after the fact, yes; at the start, no.'

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose view is this)?

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between לכתחילה and דיעבד is the key to matching the תרומה משנה with one of the views about hearing one's own words.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
that a deaf person who speaks but does not hear —
after the fact — yes,
from the start — no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who is the author of the משנה quoted in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that not hearing oneself is invalid at the start but valid after the fact.

steps.title: רב חסדא says the תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי. He cites the משנה where רבי יוסי says one who said שמע without hearing it did not fulfill his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי. As we learned: One who says שמע and did not let his own ear hear it has fulfilled his obligation. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: He has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an answer to the question from step 21. רב חסדא says the תרומה משנה matches רבי יוסי's view in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that hearing your own words really matters. That fits the תרומה משנה, which says a deaf person should not separate תרומה at the start. רבי יהודה says hearing does not matter at all for שמע, so he seems less likely to be the source of the 'not at the start' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Made it heard by his own ear
An אמורא who gives the answer here

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. רבי יהודה says he DID fulfill his obligation even without hearing. רבי יוסי says he did NOT.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is Rabbi Yosei,
as we learned: One who recites Shema
and did not make it audible to his ear — he fulfilled it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: He did not fulfill it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21 about whose view the תרומה משנה follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי, who requires hearing one's own words.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי still accepts תרומה after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says 'not fulfilled' only for שמע, which is from the Torah. For תרומה, the concern is only the ברכה, which is rabbinic, and the תרומה does not depend on the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי only said 'he did not fulfill it' about קריאת שמע, which is from the Torah. But with תרומה, the issue is only because of the ברכה. The ברכה is only rabbinic, and the matter does not depend on the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא fixes a problem with his own answer. רבי יוסי says hearing is required even after the fact, yet the תרומה משנה accepts it after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמע, hearing is part of the Torah obligation itself, so without hearing there is no קריאת שמע at all. For תרומה, the deaf person's only problem is that he cannot hear his own ברכה. The ברכה is rabbinic, and the separation of תרומה works even with no ברכה. So we tell him not to do it at the start, but once done, it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this in this specific case
A blessing (here, the one said before separating תרומה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: a missing rabbinic ברכה does not cancel the actual מצוה act.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֹא יָצָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only said 'he did not fulfill it'
regarding the recitation of Shema, which is from the Torah,
but teruma — the issue is because of the blessing,
and the blessing is rabbinic,
and the matter does not depend on the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רב חסדא's answer fits the תרומה משנה's 'after the fact it counts' ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between a Torah obligation (שמע) and a rabbinic add-on (the ברכה on תרומה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוסי says 'not fulfilled' even after the fact, he should also invalidate a deaf person's תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For תרומה, only the rabbinic ברכה is affected, and the separation does not depend on it, so it counts after the fact.

steps.title: Maybe the תרומה משנה follows רבי יהודה instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: how do we know it is רבי יוסי? Perhaps רבי יהודה also holds that for שמע, not hearing is fine only after the fact, but not at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you know it is רבי יוסי? Maybe it is רבי יהודה, and he says about קריאת שמע too: after the fact, yes; at the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's answer. It suggests the תרומה משנה could just as easily match רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומה משנה's rule is 'not at the start, but valid after the fact.' If רבי יהודה holds the same pattern for שמע, his view fits the תרומה משנה perfectly, with no need for the ברכה explanation. So רב חסדא's choice of רבי יוסי is not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know?

phrases.english: And from where do you know it is Rabbi Yosei?
Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehuda?
And he says regarding the recitation of Shema too:
after the fact — yes; at the start — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא, דִּילְמָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's identification of the תרומה משנה with רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה holds 'valid after the fact, not at the start' for שמע, he matches the תרומה משנה exactly. So there is no proof it is רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Proof from the word ״הקורא״ in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The challenger supports his idea: the משנה says ״הקורא״, 'one who recited,' which is after-the-fact language. That suggests רבי יהודה allows it only after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is so, since the משנה teaches ״הקורא״, 'one who recites.' This implies: after the fact, yes; at the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger brings support for his suggestion about רבי יהודה. He points to the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say 'one may recite without hearing.' It said 'one who recited,' describing something already done. That wording hints that even רבי יהודה only accepts it after the fact. That would make his view match the תרומה משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that this is so (introduces a support)
One who recites / recited (describes an act already done)

phrases.english: Know this, since it teaches: 'One who recites,'
meaning after the fact — yes; at the start — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the challenge in step 24 with a proof from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה allows not hearing only after the fact, not at the start
steps.raayaSupportSource: The after-the-fact wording ״הקורא״ in the משנה about שמע

steps.title: The word ״הקורא״ is there to show רבי יוסי's strong view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה said ״הקורא״ to show that רבי יוסי invalidates it even after the fact. רבי יהודה himself allows it even at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: The fact that the משנה teaches ״הקורא״ is to show you how far רבי יוסי goes, since he says it does not count even after the fact. Because if it were only about רבי יהודה, he would fulfill his obligation even at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the word ״הקורא״. It explains why the משנה used that wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The after-the-fact wording was chosen for רבי יוסי's sake. It shows that he says 'not fulfilled' even when the act is already done, which is a strong position. It tells us nothing about רבי יהודה, who allows not hearing even at the start. So the proof that רבי יהודה matches the תרומה משנה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength of his view (how far he goes)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: hearing yourself is not needed for שמע, even at the start. רבי יוסי: without hearing, you did not fulfill it, even after the fact. The משנה's word ״הקורא״ was chosen to show how strong רבי יוסי's view is.
steps.confusionAlert: The word ״הקורא״ looks like it limits רבי יהודה to after-the-fact cases. The גמרא says no: it is there to highlight רבי יוסי's strong view.

phrases.english: They say: That which it teaches 'One who recites'
is to show you the strength of Rabbi Yosei's view,
who says that even after the fact, no.
For if it were Rabbi Yehuda,
even at the start he fulfills his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from ״הקורא״ in step 25, which weakens the challenge to רב חסדא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה's wording, not the משנה itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The after-the-fact wording was chosen to highlight רבי יוסי's strong view, not to limit רבי יהודה, who allows it even at the start.

steps.title: A challenge from the ברכת המזון ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the approach that put the תרומה משנה like רבי יוסי. It brings a ברייתא: one should not say ברכת המזון in his heart, but if he did, he fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the משנה? Like רבי יוסי? But what about the ברייתא that teaches: A person should not say ברכת המזון in his heart, and if he did say it that way, he fulfilled his obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer by bringing a new source, a ברייתא about ברכת המזון. This step sets up the source; the next step shows why it causes a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה משנה is רבי יוסי, then by step 26 רבי יהודה allows silent recitation even from the start. The ברייתא gives a middle ruling: not from the start, but valid after the fact. ברכת המזון is from the Torah, just like שמע, so it is a fair comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessings after a meal, which are a Torah obligation
In his heart, meaning silently, without hearing himself

phrases.english: How did you establish it — like Rabbi Yosei?
phrases.notes: Refers to the תרומה משנה from step 22.

phrases.english: But then, what about that which was taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְבָרֵךְ אָדָם בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן בְּלִבּוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not recite Grace after Meals in his heart,
and if he did recite it that way — he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the outcome of step 26, which made רבי יהודה allow silent recitation even from the start.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי, and the resulting view of רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules 'not from the start, but valid after the fact' for a Torah blessing. That ruling must belong to someone, and under the current approach no one holds it.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits neither רבי יוסי nor רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא is. It cannot be רבי יהודה, who allows silent recitation even from the start. It cannot be רבי יוסי, who says it does not count even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Not רבי יוסי and not רבי יהודה. If it is רבי יהודה, didn't he say it works even from the start? If it is רבי יוסי, it does not work even after the fact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the ברייתא is a problem. Under the current approach, its middle ruling has no one who holds it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה (as just explained) would not say 'do not do it.' רבי יוסי would not say 'if he did it, it counts.' Only a view of 'not from the start, but valid after the fact' fits the ברייתא, and nobody holds that view right now.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, the proper way to act
After the fact, once it was already done

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Whose is it? Neither Rabbi Yosei nor Rabbi Yehuda.
For if it is Rabbi Yehuda —
didn't he say that even from the start, one fulfills the obligation?
phrases.notes: This is how step 26 explained רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא!
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yosei, even after the fact it does not count!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by showing the ברייתא from step 27 has no owner.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רבי יהודה from step 26 (valid even from the start)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's ruling, 'not from the start, but valid after the fact,' fits neither opinion as currently explained, so the explanation must be wrong.

steps.title: Back to: רבי יהודה allows it only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is רבי יהודה, who holds that silent recitation counts after the fact but should not be done from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must we say? It is רבי יהודה, and after the fact, yes, it counts; from the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is forced to return to the earlier idea from step 24: רבי יהודה allows it only after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This drops the reading from step 26 that רבי יהודה allows it even from the start. Now the ברכת המזון ברייתא fits רבי יהודה perfectly. It also means the תרומה משנה ('should not separate from the start') could match רבי יהודה too, so we no longer need רבי יוסי for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must we say? This introduces a forced conclusion.

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא says that according to רבי יהודה, reciting without hearing yourself counts דיעבד but should not be done לכתחלה. According to רבי יוסי, it does not count even דיעבד. This is not the last word: step 30 challenges it, and step 32 revises רבי יהודה's own view.

phrases.english: Rather, what must we say? It is Rabbi Yehuda.
And after the fact — yes; from the start — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from step 28 by going back to the reading of רבי יהודה from steps 24 and 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה: silent recitation counts דיעבד only, not לכתחלה.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: a חרש may separate תרומה from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new ברייתא: a חרש who speaks but cannot hear may separate תרומה even from the start. Whose view is that?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא taught by רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי: A deaf person who speaks but does not hear may separate תרומה even from the start. Whose view is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new conclusion with another ברייתא. It asks whose opinion this ברייתא can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that רבי יהודה allows not hearing only after the fact, who would let a חרש separate תרומה from the start? A חרש cannot hear his own ברכה. This ruling seems to fit neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי, so it reopens the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf person who can speak but cannot hear
Separates תרומה (the portion of produce given to a כהן)

phrases.english: But what about that which was taught by

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi:
A deaf person who speaks but does not hear —
may separate teruma from the start. Whose view is this?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people named רבי יהודה. The one who teaches this ברייתא is רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, a later אמורא. He is not the תנא רבי יהודה whose opinion is being discussed.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְתָנֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 29 with a ברייתא that allows a חרש to separate תרומה from the start.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יהודה allows not hearing only after the fact
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even רבי יהודה does not allow it from the start, then the ruling that a חרש may separate תרומה from the start seems to have no one who holds it.

steps.title: The deaf-person ruling fits neither תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem. The ruling that a חרש may separate תרומה from the start matches neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי. If it is רבי יהודה, didn't he say that after the fact it counts, but from the start it should not be done? If it is רבי יוסי, didn't he say it does not count even after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from the previous step. It shows why the ברייתא about a חרש separating תרומה has no clear author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 explained that רבי יהודה allows unheard recitation only after the fact. The חרש ברייתא allows it even from the start, so it cannot be his view. רבי יוסי is even stricter, since he says it does not count even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact: once the act is already done
From the start: the proper way to act before doing anything

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. דיעבד asks 'does it count if you already did it?' לכתחילה asks 'may you do it this way in the first place?' The whole סוגיא depends on keeping these apart.

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Neither Rabbi Yehuda nor Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: The ruling allowing a deaf person to separate teruma from the start fits neither of them.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda —

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר דִּיעֲבַד אִין, לְכַתְּחִלָּה לָא.
phrases.english: didn't he say: after the fact, yes; from the start, no?
If it is Rabbi Yosei —
didn't he say: even after the fact, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question opened in step 30 by laying out why neither תנא fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא allowing a חרש to separate תרומה even from the start
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה (as explained in step 29) allows it only after the fact. רבי יוסי does not allow it even after the fact. So no known תנא allows it from the start.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's own view versus his teacher's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חרש ברייתא really is רבי יהודה, who allows it even from the start. The ברכת המזון ברייתא reflects the view of his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is רבי יהודה, and he allows it even from the start. There is no contradiction: this ruling is his own view, and that ruling is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רבי יהודה reported two different opinions. One is his own, and one is his teacher's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his own view, רבי יהודה holds that unheard recitation is fine even from the start, so the חרש ברייתא is his. The 'only after the fact' ruling (the ברכת המזון ברייתא) records what his teacher held. The contradiction disappears because the two rulings come from two different people.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (we return to the original idea)
And it is not difficult: there is no contradiction

phrases.english: Rather, it is actually Rabbi Yehuda,
and he allows it even from the start.
And it is not difficult:
this is his own view; that is his teacher's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting attribution: two rulings are assigned to two different authorities (the student and his teacher).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות reflect רבי יהודה's single personal view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חרש ברייתא is רבי יהודה's own view, which allows it even from the start. The ברכת המזון ברייתא is his teacher's view, which allows it only after the fact.

steps.title: Source showing the teacher's view and רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source in which רבי יהודה reports his teacher רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view that one must make קריאת שמע audible, and רבי מאיר disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, 'One who reads שמע must make it heard to his own ears, as it says, “Hear, O Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One.”' רבי מאיר said to him, 'But it says, “which I command you today, upon your heart.” The words follow the intention of the heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that רבי יהודה had a teacher who required hearing one's words. This supports the answer in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns from the word 'שמע' ('hear') that one should make the words audible. The word 'צריך' ('must') sets this as the proper way from the start, though it still counts after the fact. רבי מאיר learns from 'על לבבך' that what matters is the heart's intention, so hearing is not needed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He must make it audible to his own ears

steps.whyThisMatters: This source lays out the three positions in play: the teacher (should be heard), רבי יהודה's own view, and רבי מאיר (the heart alone is enough). The next step uses רבי מאיר's position to build a second answer.

phrases.english: As we learned:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
One who reads Shema
must make it heard to his own ear,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״.
phrases.english: as it says: “Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One.”
phrases.notes: The word 'Hear' is read as a requirement to make the words audible.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said to him:
But it says:
“Which I command you today, upon your heart” —

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר כַּוָּנַת הַלֵּב הֵן הֵן הַדְּבָרִים.
phrases.english: the words follow the intention of the heart.
phrases.notes: So hearing is not needed, even from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 32 by showing that רבי יהודה reported his teacher's view on this exact question.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's teacher held one should make his words audible (so it counts only after the fact if he did not)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source in which רבי יהודה quotes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, with רבי מאיר disagreeing

steps.title: Second answer: רבי מאיר versus רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Now that the full source is quoted, the גמרא offers another answer. Even if רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher, the חרש ברייתא follows רבי מאיר and the ברכת המזון ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say that רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher. There is still no contradiction: this ruling is רבי מאיר's, and that ruling is רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, alternative answer to the challenge in step 31. It uses רבי מאיר's opinion from the source just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the heart's intention is what matters, so a חרש may separate תרומה even from the start. That is the חרש ברייתא. רבי יהודה can then agree with his teacher (only after the fact), which is the ברכת המזון ברייתא. With this answer, we no longer need to say רבי יהודה disagrees with his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this point

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the חרש ברייתא: (1) it is רבי יהודה's own view, and the 'after the fact only' ruling is his teacher's; or (2) it is רבי מאיר's view, and רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
you can even say
that Rabbi Yehuda holds like his teacher.
And it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Meir; that is Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: The חרש/תרומה ruling follows רבי מאיר; the ברכת המזון ruling follows רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second resolution, drawing on רבי מאיר's view revealed in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning one ruling to a different תנא (רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We had to say רבי יהודה disagrees with his teacher in order to explain the חרש ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חרש ברייתא follows רבי מאיר (heart intention alone is enough). רבי יהודה can agree with his teacher, and the ברכת המזון ברייתא is his.

steps.title: New source: who may read the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a parallel discussion by quoting a משנה in מסכת מגילה. Everyone may read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן, and רבי יהודה allows a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: everyone is fit to read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן. And רבי יהודה says a קטן is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new, related discussion. It quotes a משנה that lists a חרש as unfit to read the מגילה, and that will be analyzed next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה also deals with a חרש, the same person at the center of our סוגיא. The next step asks whose view this משנה follows, since it says a חרש may not read the מגילה. That connects to the debate about whether one must hear one's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (in a משנה elsewhere)
The Scroll of Esther, read on Purim
A deaf person, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor

phrases.english: We learned there:
All are fit to read the Megillah,
except a deaf person, an imbecile, and a minor.
And Rabbi Yehuda deems a minor fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִים לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, parallel discussion about a חרש in the context of reading the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All are fit to read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן.

steps.title: Who holds a deaf person's reading is invalid even after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא stands behind the משנה in מגילה, which seems to rule that a חרש's reading does not count even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that a חרש's reading does not count, even after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the משנה in מגילה that disqualifies a חרש. It is setting up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the חרש together with the שוטה and the קטן. Those two cannot fulfill the obligation at all. So the גמרא assumes the חרש is also invalid even בדיעבד, not just לכתחילה. The question is which תנא would hold such a strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (the author of this teaching)?
After the fact (once it was already done)
Also not (it doesn't count even then)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two levels apart. לכתחילה means 'from the start, should he do it?' בדיעבד means 'if he already did it, does it count?' The question here is about the stricter level: it does not count even after the fact.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
who holds that a deaf person, even after the fact, does not [fulfill the obligation]?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תָּנָא חֵרֵשׁ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the מגילה משנה quoted in step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who invalidates a חרש's reading even בדיעבד.

steps.title: רב מתנה: It is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה answers that the משנה in מגילה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers the question. The strict view about a חרש belongs to רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי is the תנא who requires a person to hear his own words for the מצוה to count. A חרש cannot hear himself. So by רבי יוסי's view, his reading fails even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
It is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מגילה משנה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Proof from our משנה: רבי יוסי requires hearing oneself
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה brings support from our משנה. רבי יהודה holds that one who reads שמע without hearing himself has fulfilled his obligation. רבי יוסי holds he has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who reads שמע but did not make it audible to his own ear has fulfilled his obligation. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: He has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה shows where רבי יוסי's strict view comes from. It is stated in our own משנה about קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that if a person did not hear his own reading, it does not count even after the fact. A חרש can never hear himself. So under רבי יוסי his reading is invalid בדיעבד, which matches the מגילה משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Made it audible to his own ear

phrases.english: As we learned: One who recites Shema
and did not make it audible to his own ear has fulfilled his obligation,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: He has not fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: This is the key line. רבי יוסי invalidates the reading even after the fact.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאׇזְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the textual basis for רב מתנה's identification in step 37.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי holds an inaudible reading is invalid even בדיעבד, and so he would invalidate a חרש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה in ברכות, the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about reading שמע without hearing oneself.

steps.title: How do we know it is רבי יוסי and invalid even after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רב מתנה's identification. How do we know the משנה follows רבי יוסי and means the reading fails even after the fact?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know that it is רבי יוסי, and that even after the fact it does not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב מתנה's assumption. This line is setting up the next move, which will offer a different way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה's answer depended on assuming the מגילה משנה means 'invalid even בדיעבד.' The גמרא now asks what proves that assumption. Perhaps the משנה only means a חרש should not read לכתחילה. If so, it could follow רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: From where do you know that it is Rabbi Yosei
and that even after the fact it is also not [valid],

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא וְדִיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רב מתנה's answer in steps 37–38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the מגילה משנה invalidates a חרש even בדיעבד, and therefore follows רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the משנה's wording forces the בדיעבד reading. It may only mean 'not לכתחילה,' which would fit רבי יהודה.
